# Problem 6: three correctness faults, pick one fix each

Scope: behaviour corrections, not optimizations. None of these change the average frame cost at the measured hotspots (About bottom avg 30.8ms is untouched); fault 2 removes wasted per-lantern math in the specific case where the cursor is gone. Every claim below is labeled MEASURED (from the numbers in the brief or code read at file:line) or INFERENCE.

---

## Fault 1: the water runs on frames, not time

**The bug (MEASURED).** `_javascript/three-background-scene.js:126` wraps the mirror as `{ update: () => { if (mirroredSurface) mirroredSurface.update(); } }`, dropping `normalizedDelta`. `_javascript/shader/mirroredSurface.js:292-293` defaults it to 1.0, so `this.time` advances 0.016 per frame regardless of real time. Consequences, tied to the measured numbers:

- At the About-page bottom, the one place water fills the view, weak machines measured 30fps. There the water clock runs at 0.48 units/s instead of the tuned 0.96, so a weak-machine visitor sees waves at half speed and a click ripple that lives ~8.3 real seconds instead of 4 (`uRippleLife` 4.0 at mirroredSurface.js:282). MEASURED.
- On 120Hz monitors everything doubles. MEASURED from the code path.
- `getActiveRipple()` (mirroredSurface.js:371-376) reports ripple age in this same warped clock, so the future character's "watch the water" timing inherits the bug. MEASURED (code).

Every other updatable already receives and uses the delta: `lanternController.update(normalizedDelta)` at lantern-controller.js:141, the loop computes it at three-shared.js:344. The water is the only frame-locked module in the scene.

### Option A: pass the delta through the wrapper

```diff
--- _javascript/three-background-scene.js
@@ line 126
-  { update: () => { if (mirroredSurface) mirroredSurface.update(); } },
+  { update: (nd) => { if (mirroredSurface) mirroredSurface.update(nd); } },
```

- **Frame saving:** none, same work per frame.
- **Visual risk: subtle, and only off-60Hz.** On any 60Hz machine (including the RTX 3080 that measured 4.2ms) `nd` averages 1.0 and nothing changes. On 30fps machines waves speed UP to the tuned rate, on 120Hz they slow DOWN to it. That is the correction.
- **Line delta:** 0 (one line modified).
- **Prefer when:** you want the fix to use the exact plumbing every other module already uses, one clock for the whole scene.

### Option B: drive the clock from performance.now() inside update

```diff
--- _javascript/shader/mirroredSurface.js
@@ line 24 (constructor)
     this.time = 0;
+    this._clockStart = performance.now();
@@ lines 292-294
-  update(normalizedDelta = 1.0) {
-    this.time += normalizedDelta * 0.016;
+  update() {
+    // Wall clock at the rate the tuning passes judged: 0.016/frame at 60fps = 0.00096 per ms.
+    this.time = (performance.now() - this._clockStart) * 0.00096;
     this.material.uniforms.uTime.value = this.time;
```

- **Frame saving:** none.
- **Visual risk: subtle,** same framerate consequences as A, plus one extra: the clock keeps running while the tab is hidden (the loop stops at three-shared.js:360-364), so waves jump ahead and a mid-flight ripple can expire during a hidden tab. Invisible in practice, nobody sees a hidden tab.
- **Line delta:** +2, plus a magic constant (0.00096) that needs its comment forever.
- **Prefer when:** you want water timing immune to any future loop change, at the cost of a second clock source.

**My pick: A.** One token of change, zero new lines (D5 clean, B adds two), and it keeps the scene on one clock discipline, the lanterns already run delta-correct and the water joins them instead of getting a private clock at a rate (0.00096/ms) that exists nowhere else in the codebase.

**Rod looks at X once:** the About water after the fix. `waveSpeed: 1.5` (three-background-scene.js:52) was tuned by eye; if Rod's monitor is 60Hz the fix changes nothing on his screen and the tune stands. If his monitor runs above 60Hz, the water he tuned was running fast and the fix will visibly slow it, then `waveSpeed` is the one knob to re-tune.

## Fault 2: lanterns dodge a phantom cursor

**The bug (MEASURED).** `lantern-controller.js:51` listens for `mouseleave` on `window`. `mouseleave` does not bubble and never targets `window`, so the listener never fires. After the first `mousemove` (document listener, line 37) `isMouseOverCanvas` is true forever: every frame pays `getWorldPosition` + ray-plane intersect per lantern (lines 182-186) and the parting field holds lanterns leaned away from wherever the cursor last was. Two extra notes from the code:

- On touch devices a tap fires one synthesized `mousemove` and never any `mouseleave`, so every phone visitor arms the per-ember math permanently at the tap point. The brief's mobile risk is exactly weak-CPU JS cost, and minimal pages run 35 embers (three-background-minimal.js:34). MEASURED (code) + MEASURED (mobile risk note).
- The codebase already contains the correct desktop pattern: mouse-trail.js:260 uses `document.addEventListener('mouseleave', ...)`, which does fire (document is in the leave chain).

### Option A: mouseleave on the document

```diff
--- _javascript/lantern-controller.js
@@ lines 51-53
-    window.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {
+    // mouseleave never targets window, so this listener was dead and the flag stuck true forever.
+    document.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {
       this.isMouseOverCanvas = false;
     });
```

- **Compat:** universal, and matches the house precedent at mouse-trail.js:260.
- **Line delta:** +1 (the comment).
- **Misses:** touch. Phones keep the stuck flag after every tap.
- **Prefer when:** you want the one-word fix that mirrors mouse-trail exactly and accept the phone gap.

### Option B: pointerout with no relatedTarget

```diff
--- _javascript/lantern-controller.js
@@ lines 51-53
-    window.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {
-      this.isMouseOverCanvas = false;
-    });
+    // mouseleave never targets window, so the old listener was dead and the flag stuck true forever.
+    // pointerout bubbles; relatedTarget is null only when the pointer left the page or a touch lifted.
+    window.addEventListener('pointerout', (event) => {
+      if (!event.relatedTarget) this.isMouseOverCanvas = false;
+    });
```

- **Compat:** pointer events are in every browser since Safari 13 (2019), and this codebase already relies on them (`pointerdown`/`pointerup` at three-background-scene.js:70-71). Element-to-element moves inside the page have a non-null `relatedTarget` and are correctly ignored.
- **Line delta:** +2 (comments; code is 3 lines replacing 3).
- **Covers:** desktop leave AND touch lift, `pointerout` fires with null `relatedTarget` after every tap, which clears the phone case Option A misses.
- **Prefer when:** you want one listener that fixes both desktop and the phone-tap leak.

### Option C: Option B plus a window blur companion

```diff
   (Option B diff, plus:)
+    window.addEventListener('blur', () => { this.isMouseOverCanvas = false; });
```

- **What it adds:** alt-tab to another OS window while the page stays visible on screen (the loop keeps running there, `visibilitychange` at three-shared.js:377 only stops it when the tab itself is hidden). Without blur the lanterns hold the dodge until the cursor next moves.
- **Line delta:** +1 over B.
- **D5 check:** it is a guard for a rare case that self-heals on the next real mousemove, and I would not add it. Listed because the brief asked.

**Least code:** A (one word). **My pick: B**, the +2 comment lines buy the touch fix on precisely the devices the measurements flag for CPU cost; A leaves phones permanently paying the loop.

- **Frame saving:** INFERENCE, under 0.5ms desktop, up to ~1ms at the 4x weak-CPU proxy on About (25 embers + the FBX lantern meshes each pay lines 182-186 per frame today whenever the cursor is anywhere, fixed: only while it is actually over the page). On phones it retires the 35-ember math after every tap.
- **Visual change a visitor sees:** today lanterns lean away from a cursor that left the window, forever. Fixed: within about a second of the cursor leaving (the `returnSpeed` easing, lines 287-294) everything drifts home to its base float. On phones, embers stop permanently avoiding the last tap.
- **Rod looks at X once:** on About, park the cursor in a lantern cluster, slide it off the window edge, the cluster should breathe back to rest. That settling is the new, correct behaviour.

## Fault 3: ember pages scroll at the wrong rate after resize or rotate

**The bug (MEASURED).** `three-shared.js:313-330` `setupScrollLockedCamera` captures `worldPerPixelY` once. The returned `updateMapper` (:325-329) is called by nothing, the only caller discards the handle (`three-background-minimal.js:78`, the comment even says so). On resize, `updateCameraFOV` (three-shared.js:107) flips fov 55/80 and `innerHeight` changes, so the scroll-to-world rate goes stale. Rotating a phone flips fov alone by tan(40)/tan(27.5) = 1.61x (MEASURED from the constants), so after a rotate the embers scroll past at ~1.6x the wrong rate on every post and section page.

### Option A: delete the dead code, keep the bug

```diff
--- _javascript/three-shared.js
@@ lines 321-330
   window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
   onScroll();
-
-  return {
-    updateMapper() {
-      const newMapper = screenToWorldMapper(camera);
-      mapper.worldPerPixelY = newMapper.worldPerPixelY;
-    },
-  };
 }
```

- **Line delta:** -7. Honest: the code claims a capability nothing uses.
- **Visual risk:** none, it changes nothing. The rotate bug stays.
- **Prefer when:** you decide mid-read rotation is not worth handling and want the codebase to stop pretending it is.

### Option B: wire updateMapper through the existing resize hook

Three small diffs. Two of them are load-bearing, not optional:

**B1, the call site** (three-background-minimal.js:78-81):
```diff
-setupScrollLockedCamera(camera);   /* side effect only, nothing reads the handle */
+const { updateMapper } = setupScrollLockedCamera(camera);
 
 /* Resize */
-setupResizeHandler(camera, renderer, composer, lanternController);
+setupResizeHandler(camera, renderer, composer, lanternController, {
+  updateScrollHeight: updateMapper,
+});
```

**B2, the hook must run AFTER the FOV update** (three-shared.js:222-226). As the handler stands, the hook runs first (line 223) and `updateCameraFOV` runs after it, so on a rotate `updateMapper` would read the OLD fov and miss the 1.61x error, the biggest part of the bug. Moving it is safe for the About page: its hook (`recalc`, three-shared.js:175-177) reads only `scrollHeight` and `innerHeight`, order-independent, and its ResizeObserver (:195-197) re-runs it anyway. MEASURED (code).
```diff
     resizeTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
-      if (options.updateScrollHeight) options.updateScrollHeight();
       updateCameraFOV(camera);
       camera.aspect = window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight;
       camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
+      // After the FOV/aspect update, so scroll hooks read the camera the page will render with.
+      if (options.updateScrollHeight) options.updateScrollHeight();
```

**B3, snap to the corrected position** (three-shared.js:324-330). Without this, a visitor who resizes and does not scroll keeps the stale camera Y until the next 1px scroll:
```diff
   return {
     updateMapper() {
-      const newMapper = screenToWorldMapper(camera);
-      mapper.worldPerPixelY = newMapper.worldPerPixelY;
+      mapper.worldPerPixelY = screenToWorldMapper(camera).worldPerPixelY;
+      onScroll();   // apply the corrected rate now, not at the next scroll event
     },
   };
```

- **Line delta:** +4 across two files (mostly comments; B3 is net 0). D5 justification: no new mechanism, it reuses the one resize hook that already exists, and the lines are a behaviour fix, not an optimization. D5 targets optimizations.
- **Frame saving:** none, runs once per resize behind the existing 100ms debounce (three-shared.js:222).
- **Visual risk: visible only after a resize or rotate,** which is the point: embers scroll past at the same rate as the page instead of up to 1.61x off, plus a one-time reposition at resize (from B3, inside the debounce, reads as part of the reflow).
- **Rename variant** (the hook name lies, it says scroll height but here it updates the pixel-to-world scale): rename the option key to `updateScrollMapping` in exactly three places, three-shared.js:223 (both mentions), three-background-scene.js:117 (`updateScrollMapping: updateScrollHeight,`), and B1 above. Net 0 lines, and both callers' meaning ("recompute how scroll maps to the camera") now matches the name. Take it or leave it independently of B.
- **Prefer when:** you want rotate/resize to actually be correct on every post and section page, for four lines.

### Option C: also re-spawn the ember spread on resize

`spawnElements` (three-background-minimal.js:39-45) computes the ember band from page height at load. After a rotate the band no longer matches the reflowed page, so long pages can run out of embers near the bottom. Fixing it needs each ember to remember its page fraction and a respan pass rewriting `basePosition.y` on resize, ~10 new lines that fight `addLantern`'s captured base position (lantern-controller.js:75).

- **Verdict: scope creep.** The symptom (slightly thinner ember coverage at the bottom, only after a mid-read rotate) is mild, mobile already pins 16.7 (MEASURED), and the cost is real mechanism. Log it to `redesign-lab/feature-backlog.md`, do not build it here.

**My pick: B** (B1+B2+B3 together, they are one fix; the naive B1-only wiring leaves the rotate case broken because of the hook ordering). Rename variant optional. C logged, not built.

**Rod looks at X once:** open any post page, resize the browser window tall-to-short, then scroll: embers should track the page at the same relative rate as before the resize instead of drifting fast.

---

**Recommendation: 1A + 2B + 3B.** Net line delta about +6 across three files, zero change on a 60Hz desktop with the cursor over the page, and all three clocks (water time, cursor presence, scroll rate) become true on the 30fps and phone hardware the measurements flagged.
